newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean defector to South shot and injured.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector to South shot and injured.

text.p: A North Korean defector to South Korea has been shot and injured by two gunmen in an attack apparently ordered by the communist state, a senior police officer told Reuters.
The defector, Li Il-nam (known in South Korea as Lee Han-yong), is a nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's girlfriend, he said.

The police officer said Li was shot outside his home at Bundang, just south of the capital Seoul, late on Saturday evening. A nurse at a nearby hospital said he later underwent surgery but she gave no details of his condition.

The officer, who asked not to be identified, said he suspected the gunmen were North Korean agents ordered to shoot Li as a warning to the South following the defection of a high North Korean official, now holed up in the South Korean mission in Beijing. The gunmen were being sought by police.

South Korea says Hwang Jang-yop, a member of the secretariat of North Korea's ruling Workers" Party, sought political asylum in Seoul's Beijing mission after arriving there by taxi on Wednesday. North Korea insists Hwang was kidnapped by the South.
Li, 36, is the first North Korean defector to be shot in South Korea since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War, the officer said.
